title: Pancreatic beta cell function siRNA screen (Thomsen SK et al., 2016)
bodyHtml:
This table displays results from the study:

Systematic Functional Characterization of Candidate Causal Genes for Type 2 Diabetes Risk Variants.
Thomsen SK et al.
Diabetes. 2016 Dec;65(12):3805-3811. doi: 10.2337/db16-0361.
PMID: 27554474

In this study, expression of 300 candidate T2D effector genes from 75 T2D-associated loci was perturbed in the human pancreatic EndoC-βH1 cell line using small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated silencing. The effects of silencing on insulin secretion and cell number were assessed under 4 conditions: low glucose (1 mmol/L); high glucose (20 mmol/L); high glucose with the sulfonylurea tolbutamide (100 mmol/L); or high glucose with the phosphodiesterase inhibitor IBMX (100 mmol/L).

The table below lists effect sizes (% deviation from nontargeted control) for the 45 genes that were considered to be robust screening hits, with an FDR-adjusted q value <0.05 and an absolute effect size among the top 5% under at least one of the tested conditions.

View results from this study in the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas.
